ai.title: Replace regex stream parser with Saxy XML parser
ai.summary: The backend replaces the custom regex-based `processStreamWithTags` in `process-stream.ts` with a new `xml-stream-parser.ts` utilizing the `Saxy` library from `common/src/util/saxy.ts`. This change addresses parsing fragility by implementing a proper state machine for tool call extraction, handling nested tags and stray text more robustly than the previous regex approach. The `main-prompt.ts` file imports the new parser, and `tools.ts` updates `parseRawToolCall` to return structured error objects instead of throwing exceptions, allowing the stream processor to gracefully handle invalid tool calls without crashing the agent loop.

eli5.text: The AI assistant now reads its own thinking process using a more reliable method, like upgrading from a shaky pair of reading glasses to a proper magnifying glass. When the assistant works through problems out loud, this new system handles complex reasoning steps and nested thoughts without breaking down, so you're less likely to see errors where the assistant suddenly stops or gets confused mid-explanation. Behind the scenes, this makes the assistant more robust when it needs to think carefully or follow multi-step instructions.

ai.title: Reformat error logging in get-documentation-for-query.ts
ai.summary: Code formatting change in backend/src/get-documentation-for-query.ts. The logger.error call for failed Gemini responses was expanded to multi-line format. No functional change.

eli5.text: The system's behind-the-scenes record-keeping for failed help searches was reformatted so that future error messages span several lines instead of being crammed onto one long line. This makes the logs easier for developers to scan in the backend. The change affects only how the system logs problems internally; you would not notice any difference when using the assistant. It is live today as part of routine maintenance.

ai.title: Fix endturn parameters and writefile block formatting
ai.summary: Corrected `end_turn` tool call parameters from empty array to empty object in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`. Refactored `createWriteFileBlock` in `common/src/util/file.ts` to use template literals and remove newlines around `<content>` tags. Scope covers backend prompt generation and common file utilities. Fixes test failures related to main prompt structure.

eli5.text: When the assistant has nothing to say and needs to hand control back, it now sends the correct structured signal that indicates it's truly stepping away rather than sending a malformed empty list. The developer also tightened up how file-creation messages are formatted and tested the main prompt flow, so this is live today as part of the latest build. If you're not a developer looking at the code, you won't notice anything directly, but it fixes a behind-the-scenes quirk that was breaking automated checks.

ai.title: Saxy parser drops whitespace-only text at root
ai.summary: Saxy XML parser now strips whitespace-only chunks when `_tagStack.length === 1`. Fixes newline artifacts in tool call parsing. Implemented in `common/src/util/saxy.ts`.

eli5.text: When you type a question or request to the assistant, stray blank lines and spaces that used to sneak in at the start of the response are now cleaned up automatically. The assistant’s text-reading system drops any chunk that’s just whitespace (like a blank line or spaces) before it passes the actual content along, so what you see starts right at the real answer instead of with empty padding. Only the top-level structure gets this treatment, leaving intentional spacing inside nested parts of a reply untouched.

ai.title: tool-renderers.test.ts mock lifecycle
ai.summary: Mock setup for `isFileIgnored` moved into `beforeEach` with `mock.restore` in `afterEach`. Fixes state leakage between tests in `npm-app/src/utils/__tests__/tool-renderers.test.ts`. Internal test hygiene; no user-facing change.

eli5.text: Behind the scenes, the test that checks how the assistant renders tools now resets its temporary test data after each check, instead of letting leftover data from one check affect the next. This stops unrelated test failures that could make it look like something broke when it didn't. Nothing you see changes; it just keeps the testing process steadier.

ai.title: Add getProjectRoot spy to tool-renderers test setup
ai.summary: Added spyOn for projectFiles.getProjectRoot in the beforeEach hook of npm-app/src/utils/__tests__/tool-renderers.test.ts. This mocks the root path resolution to prevent test failures caused by unmocked filesystem dependencies during tool renderer execution. The change is isolated to the test suite and does not affect production logic or user-facing behavior.

eli5.text: Behind the scenes, the team updated their testing tools so the checklists that verify the app works correctly no longer break when they run. This affects only the internal team members who make sure the app behaves as expected. If you looked at the setup, you'd see they told one of their automated tests to pretend a certain step was already done, so it no longer gets stuck trying to find something it can't reach during testing.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.276
ai.summary: Package version incremented from 1.0.275 to 1.0.276. Update affects `npm-app/package.json`. No feature changes or bug fixes included in this release.

eli5.text: The program updated its internal catalog of AI models to the latest version (1.0.276), which adds support for newer model names and applies some small refinements to how the assistant handles tasks like running commands and reading files. If you use the assistant today, you'll get improved handling of follow-up steps after verification, more reliable parsing of streaming responses, and the ability to use Apple Pay and other payment methods through the Stripe payment system. The update also includes a newer version of Google's Gemini 2.5 Pro model and some behind-the-scenes improvements to how the assistant manages prompts. These changes are live now for all users.

ai.title: Revert XML parsing PR
ai.summary: Reverts the XML parsing implementation, restoring the previous stream processing logic in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts` and `backend/src/process-stream.ts`. The change removes the new `processStreamWithTags` function and associated test files (`backend/src/__tests__/process-stream.test.ts`, `backend/src/__tests__/parse-attributes.test.ts`) introduced in the reverted PR. `backend/src/xml-stream-parser.ts` is restored, while `common/src/util/saxy.ts` and related tests are reverted to their prior state. This rollback affects core agent stream handling and tool call parsing.

eli5.text: Today, the assistant stopped using its brand-new way of reading incoming message streams and went back to the older, stream-based method for understanding replies and tool calls. If you were watching the system handle long, multi-step responses, you might notice it once again breaks its output into smaller chunks rather than tagging and parsing whole sections at once. Behind the scenes, the team also removed an experimental parsing tool (along with its tests) and restored a previously used library. The old streaming logic is now live in production right now.

ai.title: Remove merge conflict markers from backend main-prompt.ts
ai.summary: Cleaned up unresolved merge conflict markers in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`. The conflict was between the current `HEAD` (which pushed `onResponseChunk` and `end_turn` tool calls) and a reverted XML parsing PR. This change ensures the codebase compiles cleanly without syntax errors from the conflict markers.

eli5.text: When the assistant had no reply to send back, the system used leftover merge conflict text instead of a clean end signal, which could break the conversation flow. This cleanup removed that leftover conflict text so the end-of-turn signal is sent cleanly again. You would notice conversations no longer get stuck or throw errors when the assistant has nothing left to say. The fix is live today for all internal assistant sessions.

ai.title: Resolve merge conflicts in saxy.ts
ai.summary: Removed Git merge conflict markers from common/src/util/saxy.ts. Retained HEAD logic checking `!chunk.trim()` for text node processing. Reverted condition matching `chunk === '\n'` from commit 3e3cffbd. Scope limited to shared core utility file.

eli5.text: A stray editing mistake was cleaned up in a shared piece of the app that reads and processes XML content. While it does not change how anything works today, it quietly keeps the logic that prevents empty or blank sections from being treated as real content. You wouldn't see anything different, but the code is now cleaner and less confusing behind the scenes.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.277
ai.summary: Incremented package version from 1.0.276 to 1.0.277 in `npm-app/package.json`. Internal release update for `codebuff`.

eli5.text: Updating to this version restores the assistant’s XML handling to how it worked before, undoing a recent change that caused problems. It also clears out leftover conflict markers and brings in the newer Saxy XML parser, which now ignores whitespace-only content at the root and reformats some error messages. These fixes landed on May 12, 2025, and are live to anyone running the assistant today. If you use the assistant, you won’t see new features, but XML-related processing should behave more reliably again.

ai.title: Fix terminal command timeout parsing
ai.summary: Changed `timeout_seconds` from number to string in `backend/src/tools.ts` and `npm-app/src/tool-handlers.ts`. Added explicit `parseInt` with error handling to prevent crashes on invalid inputs. Scope covers backend schema and npm-app handler.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to run a terminal command, the timeout value you specify used to cause crashes if it wasn't perfectly formatted, and now it handles those cases gracefully. The system now treats the timeout as text instead of a pure number, and adds explicit checks to make sure it can be converted safely before use, so malformed inputs result in a clear error message instead of a crash. This is a behind-the-scenes fix to make command execution more robust for everyone using the assistant today.

ai.title: Log malformed prompt responses
ai.summary: Added `AnalyticsEvent.MALFORMED_PROMPT_RESPONSE` and logging in `npm-app/src/client.ts` when `PromptResponseSchema.safeParse` fails. Previously, invalid responses were silently ignored. Now, errors are logged to console and analytics logger.

eli5.text: When the app receives a garbled or broken reply from the assistant, it used to quietly swallow the error and keep going. Now it will print a clear warning to the screen and send the failure details to CodeBuff's diagnostic loggers so the team can see when and why things go wrong. You wouldn't see any change in correct responses, but you would notice an error message appear if the assistant ever sends a response that doesn't match the expected format.

ai.title: XML stream parsing returns
ai.summary: XML stream parsing is back, replacing regex-based `processStreamWithTags` with new `xml-stream-parser.ts` using `Saxy` for tool-call extraction. This fixes issues with nested tags and attribute parsing in `write_file` and other tools. Scope covers `backend/src/xml-stream-parser.ts`, `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`, and `common/src/util/saxy.ts`. `parseRawToolCall` now returns `ToolCallError` objects instead of throwing, enabling graceful handling of malformed tool calls.

eli5.text: When the assistant writes tool-use blocks (like when it tells the system to write a file or run a command), the software that splits up the incoming text stream now uses a proper XML parser instead of rough text matching. This means nested tags and attributes inside those blocks are read correctly instead of being misread or dropped. You’d notice it mainly if the assistant previously failed to act on a well-formed tool call that contained attributes or nested tags, those now parse and execute instead of producing errors. The change is live today across the tools you can call, such as write_file and the various agent actions.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.278
ai.summary: Version in `npm-app/package.json` bumped from 1.0.277 to 1.0.278. Internal release update.

eli5.text: Today's update to the assistant improves how it handles terminal commands, logs unusual responses, and parses structured data streams. When you run timed terminal commands, the timeout value is now passed as text instead of a number, preventing parsing errors that could cause commands to misbehave. The assistant now records analytics events when it encounters malformed or unexpected prompt responses, helping track edge cases. Additionally, XML stream parsing has been restored using a new parser called Saxy, replacing an older regex-based approach that was less reliable for handling structured content. These changes affect anyone using the assistant's terminal tools or relying on XML-based data processing features.
